The patient with alcohol-associated cirrhosis and recurrent hepatic encephalopathy, last seen in Hepatology eight months prior, presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of progressive confusion, lethargy, and difficulty speaking.
His wife reports that he has not been eating well and has been drinking alcohol more frequently.

Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg, heart rate 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, and temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F)
On examination, the patient is drowsy but arousable.
Neurological examination reveals bilateral hand tremors and flapping of the hands when the wrists are extended.
